summary: 1 blocker(s), 0 possible blocker(s), 2 warning(s), 2 context finding(s); 2 pod(s) would need to move.

ignoredPods.reason: DaemonSet pod; autoscalers do not need to reschedule it

findings.subject: Deployment/checkout/api
findings.claim: The workload sits at its HPA floor (minReplicas=3, replicas=3). HPA will not scale it lower, so its 3 pod(s) keep holding 1.5 CPU and 3.0Gi memory even when idle.
findings.meaning: These pods exist because of configuration, not load. Lowering the minimum (or scaling to zero off-hours) is what frees this capacity.

findings.subject: Deployment/checkout/api
findings.claim: Pods of this workload request more than VPA api recommends: 2 request(s) above its upper bound and 0 more than 25% above its target. The VPA is in mode Off, so it only recommends.
findings.meaning: Each pod reserves more than it is likely to use, so fewer pods fit on a node and nodes look full on paper.
unknowns: VPA recommends from recent usage; a workload with rare peaks may still need its headroom.

findings.subject: Deployment/checkout/api
findings.claim: VPA api recommends different requests, but its update mode is Off, so nothing applies them.
findings.meaning: The right size is known but not applied.

findings.subject: Pod/checkout/api-7d9f-c
findings.claim: None of the 3 other schedulable node(s) in the snapshot can take this pod. Draining this node would leave it Pending, so autoscalers keep the node.
findings.meaning: The other nodes say no because of: pod anti-affinity on 2 node(s), taint on 1 node(s).

evidence.value: pod anti-affinity on kubernetes.io/hostname: Pod/checkout/api-7d9f-a already runs there
pod anti-affinity on kubernetes.io/hostname: Pod/checkout/api-7d9f-b already runs there

alternatives: Karpenter may replace this node with a cheaper one instead of deleting it; this rule only checks moving pods onto existing nodes.
Requests may be larger than real usage; right-sizing (for example with VPA recommendations) could create room.
unknowns: Placement is a first-fit estimate by requests, largest pod first; a different packing might succeed.
Volume zones, pod priority and preemption were not evaluated.

findings.subject: Node/general-c
findings.claim: Karpenter has not marked this node consolidatable yet, so it does not consider removing or replacing it. NodePool general waits consolidateAfter (1m) after pods were last added to or removed from a node.
unknowns: Frequent pod churn on the node keeps restarting this wait.

limitations: Snapshot heuristic, not a scheduler simulation: placement checks cover node selectors, required node affinity, taints, required pod (anti-)affinity, topology spread and host ports, but not volume zones, priorities, preemption or preferred rules.
Autoscaler settings are read where the cluster exposes them (Karpenter NodePools and NodeClaims), not Cluster Autoscaler flags or node group minimums.
One point in time: PDB status, replica counts and events change.
Packing is measured with resource requests, not real usage.
Pod size is judged only where a VPA recommendation exists; other workloads are unknowns.
Read-only: KubeShrink never modifies a cluster.
